To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a virulence plsmid, Vir, associated with invasive Escherichiacoli strains confers on these strains the capacity to adhere to epithelial tissue.
the Vir plasmids from E. coli strains 711 and 711v are responsible for their adhesion to epithelial cells.

the virulence plasmids of invasive Eschericha coli are responsible for the adhesive properties of these organisms to calf intestinal brush borders and that these properties are mediated by the presence of mannosylated surface components of the bacterial cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the Vir plasmids in the pathogenicity of Escherichia Coli strains.
the adhesive properties of a transmissible pathogen associated with strains of virulent Escherichia colii.
the adhesive properties of the Vir plasmids and their possible association with the pathogenicity of strains of E. coli.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

Vir+ strains of E. coli are capable of attaching to the brush border epithelial cells in the small intestine and the trachea of calves in vitro in the presence of D-mannose, and the Vir plasmids are involved in the adhesion of the strains.
the Vir plasmids encode a mannose-sensitive haemagglutinin which mediates attachment of the Vir plasmide Escherichia to epithelial cells.
the virulence plasmids of the invasive E. coli strains 711v, H209av and S5 are responsible for the adhesive properties associated with them.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Vir plasmids of E. coli strains S5, 711v and 711v-3 confer adhesive properties upon the bacteria which enable them to attach to calf epithelia from the ileum and oesophagus.

the Vir plasmids of E. coli strains 711v, H209av and S5 possess an adhesive property associated with the ability of the strains to attach to epithelia in the presence of D-mannose, that this property is not due to a surface component of the bacterium, that it is not a heat-labile protein, that it is antigenic and that it is probably a carbohydrate.
the Vir plasmids of Escherichia strains S5, 711v and S9 are associated with the adhesive properties of the strains.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Vir+ plasmid is associated with the adhesive properties of invasive E. coli strains.
the Vir plasmids are important virulence factors in strains of E. coli that cause disease.
the Vir plasmids of E. coli are involved in the adhesion of these organisms to the intestinal mucosa and that the Vir plas-mid-encoded adhesion is mediated by a mannose-sensitive mechanism.
